topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: These opening remarks introduce the lecture topic of cancer therapy and outline the intended learning objectives.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional therapeutic modalities including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapeutics alongside associated systemic toxicities and efflux-mediated drug resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting tumor signaling dependencies and checkpoint defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic biological vulnerabilities in cancer cells, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint deficiencies, and DNA repair defects.

topics.label: Targeted kinase inhibitors and resistance pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address oncogene addiction, the design of small-molecule kinase inhibitors, and mechanisms of acquired resistance such as gatekeeper mutations and bypass signaling pathways.

topics.label: Antibody-based targeted therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the mechanisms and clinical utility of monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates designed to selectively target tumor cell-surface markers.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and cellular therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence for natural immune surveillance and evaluate immunotherapeutic strategies including immune checkpoint blockade, bispecific T-cell engagers, and CAR T-cell therapies.

topics.label: Challenges, historical progress, and future paradigms in cancer management
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate historical survival trends, ongoing clinical challenges such as tumor heterogeneity, and future directions and ethical dilemmas in oncological treatment.
